entries.note: The proposition drops 'a fair case can be made' and 'often.' The future claim explicitly says 'probably.'
Achievability asserts a possibility, not a prediction that AGI will arrive.

entries.test: Whether LLMs like ChatGPT achieve the breadth and resourcefulness of human intelligence without a fundamentally different architecture.
entries.note: 'I don’t think' expresses his negative prediction here.

entries.test: Whether subsequent LLMs reliably eliminate the specified recurring failures in reasoning, hallucination, tool use and alignment.
entries.note: The later discussion identifies the core problems.

entries.test: Whether ChatGPT had delivered the subsequently listed expectations of imminent AGI, tenfold productivity and PhD-level general competence by publication.
entries.note: The following paragraphs give concrete content to 'expectations.'

entries.test: Whether AI with human breadth and resourcefulness emerges in the near term following November 2025.
entries.note: 'Soon' supplies no fixed deadline; the separate exclusion of year-end 2025 is already due.

entries.test: The productivity gains reported in public LLM studies available by November 29, 2025, including whether any approached tenfold productivity.
entries.note: Tenfold productivity corresponds to a 900% increase, despite the source's parenthetical.

entries.test: Public surveys and corporate forecasts of expected generative-AI returns compared with subsequent reported returns.
entries.note: The normalization turns 'must have imagined' into an unqualified statement about expectations.

entries.test: Whether subsequent comparable studies corroborated the reported MIT finding that only 5% of companies obtained returns on generative-AI investment.
entries.note: The McKinsey metric quoted in support must be checked for comparability.

entries.test: Public economic analyses of whether generative-AI investment and financial exposure created substantial economy-wide downside risk at publication.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'by many accounts' and narrows being 'wrapped up' in AI and its promises to dependence.

entries.test: If the anticipated economic downturn occurs, public economic evidence showing whether the ChatGPT-centered AI boom and bust was a central contributor.
entries.note: Context gives 'at the center' a substantive economic meaning.

entries.test: Public deployment studies linking limited productivity, adoption or returns to technical unreliability, together with contemporaneous evidence of that unreliability from launch.
entries.note: 'Results' refers to the economic and productivity outcomes discussed above.

entries.test: Public evaluations of scaled models through publication documenting whether reliability, physical and psychological understanding, and hallucination problems persisted.
entries.note: The proposition extracts the technical claim without the separate claim about thousands of interlocutors.

entries.test: Comparative benchmarks and user-task studies showing whether GPT-5 and contemporary models offered better capabilities and practical utility than GPT-3.5.
entries.note: The source attributes greater impressiveness specifically to GPT-5 and greater utility to the latest models; the proposition applies both predicates to both.

entries.test: Public evaluations of the named model families against the concrete failures identified in Marcus's December 2022 predictions.
entries.note: The universal scope is Marcus's own, not an addition by the drafter.

entries.test: Public evaluations establishing whether hundreds of LLMs exhibit the recurring failure modes listed in the post.
entries.note: The surrounding insult does not erase the empirical assertion.

The proposition adds that GPT-5 lacks enormous value and asserts a causal explanation. Its hypothetical economic value if those problems had been solved is counterfactual; the unsolved-problems component alone is checkable.

entries.test: Public tests of contemporary LLM controllability, reasoning, tool use, hallucination, specialist-model performance and alignment.
entries.note: The proposition omits 'So far as I know.' That qualification does not prevent testing the reported failures.

entries.test: Public system documentation and ablation studies showing which capabilities require external calculators, interpreters or other components beyond the language model.
entries.note: 'The full solution people imagine' concerns general intelligence in context; 'solution to AI' broadens that scope.

entries.test: Longitudinal benchmark results and failure analyses showing improved scores alongside persistent reasoning, hallucination, control and alignment failures.
entries.note: The post specifies the qualitative problems being compared.
The future claim is conditional on excluding neurosymbolic systems and world models, and explicitly says 'probably.'
The conclusion links unpredictability to trust, but supplies no shared standard for 'never really trust.'
This is an overall verdict of failure that weighs costs and achievements without a shared success threshold.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and deployment evidence showing whether training and operating costs plus reliability constraints account for OpenAI's and comparable providers' lack of profits.
entries.note: Difficulty isolating the causes does not make the claim uncheckable.
The sentence is Marcus's own reaction to Brock's quotation. The drafter supplies a precise AGI endpoint for the undefined 'work.'
The normalization drops 'in my mind' and the condition that the AI situation goes belly-up. Ranking personal culpability is a judgment; the bluffing allegation also concerns private knowledge.

entries.test: Huang's public remarks and supporting evidence showing whether his argument establishes exponential capability gains or AGI from exponential compute growth.
entries.note: This evaluates the public argument rather than Huang's private intentions.

entries.test: The Census Bureau AI-adoption time series available at publication and whether it showed slowing demand inconsistent with continuing exponential growth.
entries.note: 'Shows signs of' is weaker than the normalized 'shows ... tapering off.'

entries.test: If increasing scale ceases to yield substantial capability gains, subsequent public AI-compute demand data showing whether demand declines.
entries.note: The surrounding Nvidia discussion supports interpreting demand as compute demand.
The normalization replaces the stated one-to-two-order hype comparison with generic greater scale and omits equal naïveté. The loss and damage predictions are expressly possibilities.
Calling believers fools does not itself assert both categorical propositions supplied by the drafter.

entries.test: Public studies of amateur AI-assisted development measuring prototype creation, generated-code defects and successful production hardening.
entries.note: 'Tends to' describes an empirical frequency pattern rather than merely a possible outcome.

entries.test: Public analyses linking promotional AI media coverage to increases in AI-company market valuations.
entries.note: 'Without skepticism' strengthens 'too little skepticism'; the proposition also omits the subjective characterization of the analyses.
'Maybe' makes the proposed explanation of market movements tentative.
The hypothetical public-market valuation concerns a counterfactual. The separate no-moat assertion could be tested through competitive evidence.

entries.test: Public model pricing and substitution evidence, provider profitability reports, and OpenAI financial reporting showing its monthly losses at publication.
entries.note: The scarcity of available financial disclosures does not preclude checking the claim.

entries.test: Public Gemini 3 and GPT-5 benchmark results available in November 2025 showing how many benchmarks favored Gemini 3.
entries.note: The explicit benchmark comparison gives the qualified 'seems' assertion a concrete test.

entries.test: Public valuation and profitability reports, usage trends, competitor performance and investor assessments available at publication.
entries.note: The surrounding financial and usage claims give 'hopes are slipping' an observable business meaning.

entries.test: Subsequent public evidence of continued LLM availability, falling comparable-use prices and useful deployments.
entries.note: No deadline is specified.

entries.test: Whether an LLM achieves AGI or LLM markets develop durable differentiation and pricing power inconsistent with commodity status.
entries.note: A decisive counterexample could falsify the undated 'never' claims.
'Might be like' explicitly qualifies the illustrative percentages.

entries.test: Public evaluations comparing human judgments of LLM answer plausibility with independent factual verification of those same answers.
entries.note: The plausibility-versus-accuracy comparison has a plain empirical reading.

entries.test: Comparative tests of GPT-5 and representative seven- and eight-year-olds on factual trivia and writing correct Python code.
entries.note: The next sentences explicitly supply these examples.

entries.test: Public arithmetic-reliability comparisons, documented ChatGPT hallucinations and errors, and disclosures about its training-data coverage.
entries.note: The normalization literalizes the hyperbolic 'swallowed the entire internet' and drops the judgment that these errors should be shocking.

entries.test: Public tests comparing GPT and children on novel physical, social and embodied reasoning, alongside evidence of coherent world representations.
entries.note: The specified objects, people and bodily behavior give the world-model comparison empirical content.

'I can’t imagine any could' expresses qualified disbelief, not categorical incapacity. The proposition also generalizes one child's particular achievement to children's novel physical reasoning overall.
This recommends a research direction and allocation of effort.
This combines an evaluative verdict with a recommendation to move on.
